options: Sales can continue for 28 days while a new DPS is found
All sales of alcohol must stop immediately
Only the Personal Licence holder can continue selling alcohol
The Premises Licence holder can take over automatically

bank.question: Preventing 'moral or psychological harm' to minors falls under which of the four licensing objectives?
bank.explanation: The 'Protection of Children from Harm' objective specifically addresses the physical, moral, and psychological risks to minors
options: The protection of children from harm
The prevention of crime and disorder

bank.question: How many Temporary Event Notices (TENs) can a 'non-personal licence holder' submit in a single calendar year?
bank.explanation: A person who does not hold a Personal Licence can only submit 5 TENs per calendar year

bank.question: Who can make a representation against an application to vary a Premises Licence?
bank.explanation: Any individual or organisation (e.g., local residents or businesses) can object to a variation if it impacts the licensing objectives
options: Only the Police and Environmental Health
Only people living within 100 metres of the premises
Any person, regardless of their geographic location

bank.question: When a person applies for a Personal Licence, which body has the power to object if the applicant has a relevant conviction?
bank.explanation: The Licensing Authority must notify the Police of a Personal Licence application, and only the Police can object on crime prevention grounds
options: All local residents within a 50-metre radius

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, which number is correct?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: When applying for a new Premises Licence, the public notice displayed at the premises must be printed on pale yellow paper
bank.explanation: The notice must be printed on pale blue paper, not yellow, and must be at least A4 in size

bank.question: Which type of premises is exempt from the requirement to have a Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS)?
bank.explanation: A club holding a CPC (like a British Legion or sports club) does not need a DPS because it is run by a committee rather than a commercial owner
options: A private members' club with a Club Premises Certificate
A Petrol Station shop with a licence

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, what answer should be recorded?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: Licensed premises are legally required to provide free tap water to customers upon request
bank.explanation: The mandatory conditions require that free potable (drinking) water be provided on request to customers

bank.question: What happens to a Personal Licence if the holder changes jobs and moves to a different licensed premises?
bank.explanation: The Personal Licence remains valid even if the holder leaves the trade, unless it is forfeited, suspended, or surrendered
options: It must be returned to the Home Office
It is transferred to the new employer
The holder keeps the licence; it belongs to the individual

bank.question: How long does a Personal Licence remain valid for?
bank.explanation: Personal Licences are now indefinite and do not require renewal every 10 years, as was previously the case before 2015

bank.question: A Personal Licence must be renewed every 10 years with the Licensing Authority that originally issued it
bank.explanation: Under the Licensing Act 2003, a Personal Licence is now valid indefinitely and no longer requires renewal every 10 years

bank.question: Under the Licensing Act 2003, which of the following is a mandatory requirement?
bank.explanation: The Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) must be a Personal Licence holder to be legally named on the Premises Licence
options: A Personal Licence holder must be present behind the bar at all times
The Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) must hold a Personal Licence
Every member of staff selling alcohol must hold a Personal Licence
The Premises Licence Holder must always be a Personal Licence holder

bank.question: To enter a premises used primarily for alcohol consumption, a child under 16 must be accompanied by whom?
bank.explanation: Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult if the premises is used primarily for the sale and consumption of alcohol
options: A member of the bar staff

bank.question: What is the minimum age for a staff member to sell alcohol in a supermarket, provided the sale is specifically approved by a responsible person?
bank.explanation: While the Licensing Act is federal to England and Wales, specific 'Alcohol Delivery' rules usually allow sales until 11pm if they involve off-site delivery
options: 14 or 15 years old, if they are on a training scheme
Only those who hold a Personal Licence

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, which figure applies?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: A personal licence is portable, meaning it allows the holder to be named as a DPS at any licensed premises in England and Wales
bank.explanation: A personal licence is designed to move with the individual and is not tied to a specific building or business

bank.question: Where must the 'Summary of the Premises Licence' (Part B) be kept at the premises?
bank.explanation: The Summary of the Premises Licence (Part B) must be prominently displayed so the public and authorities can see it
options: In a locked safe in the office
Prominently displayed on the premises where it can be easily read
Pinned to the back of the main entry door

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, what is the correct figure?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: What is the maximum duration for a single Temporary Event Notice (TEN)?
bank.explanation: The Maximum period for a single TEN is 168 hours (7 days). Items exceeding this require a full Premises Licence

bank.question: Under the Licensing Act 2003, which of the following is a specific offence?
bank.explanation: It is an offence to sell alcohol to a person who is drunk or to buy alcohol for someone who is already drunk
options: Selling alcohol to a person with a disability
Selling alcohol to a person who is 25 years old
Selling alcohol to a person who is already drunk
Selling alcohol to a person without a printed receipt

bank.question: A personal licence holder only needs to notify the Licensing Authority of a criminal conviction if it results in a prison sentence
bank.explanation: If a licence holder is convicted of a 'relevant offence', they must notify the Licensing Authority in writing as soon as possible

bank.question: What is the minimum age for a staff member to sell alcohol in a bar without any specific exemptions?
bank.explanation: Staff must be 18 to sell alcohol in a bar unless it is a table meal and the sale is specifically authorised by a responsible adult

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, which value completes the rule?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: What is the legal duty of a staff member regarding a customer who is clearly drunk?
bank.explanation: Allowing a person who is already drunk to remain on the premises or serving them more alcohol is a criminal offence
options: Offer them a free glass of water
Ask them to sit down for 30 minutes before buying more alcohol
Suggest they switch to low-alcohol beer
Refuse to serve them and ensure they leave or are monitored

bank.question: In a premises licensed for the sale of alcohol, who must authorise every sale of alcohol?
bank.explanation: Section 19 of the Act requires every sale of alcohol to be made or authorised by a Personal Licence holder

bank.question: Every premises licence that authorises the sale of alcohol must identify a single individual as the Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS)
bank.explanation: The DPS is the person specified on the premises licence as the individual responsible for the day-to-day running of the venue

bank.question: What are the two standard legal measures for Gin, Vodka, Rum and Whisky sold for consumption on a premises?
bank.explanation: Spirits like Gin and Vodka must be sold in quantities of 25ml or 35ml (and multiples thereof) under Weights and Measures law

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, what numerical answer is expected?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: Under the Licensing Act 2003, it is an offence to knowingly sell alcohol to someone if
bank.explanation: Knowingly allowing the sale of alcohol to any person who is drunk is a specific offence under the Licensing Act 2003
options: The person is under 21 but looks 25
The person is a local resident without ID
The person is known to be a vegetarian

bank.question: What is the legal term for a comment or objection made against a new Premises Licence application?
bank.explanation: Licensing Authorities must consider any 'relevant representation' from responsible authorities or other persons when deciding an application

bank.question: Public Safety is one of the four licensing objectives specified in the Licensing Act 2003
bank.explanation: Promoting 'Public Safety' is one of the four statutory licensing objectives that all licence holders must uphold

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of making a 'representation' regarding a Premises Licence application?
bank.explanation: Relevant representations must be based on how the application might affect one or more of the four licensing objectives
options: To suggest the prices of alcohol are too high
To complain about the competition for existing businesses
To prevent crime, disorder, or public nuisance
To request that the premises only serves local beers

bank.question: To be legally classed as 'alcohol' under the Licensing Act 2003, what must be the minimum Alcohol by Volume (ABV)?
bank.explanation: Under the Licensing Act 2003, alcohol is defined as a spirituous liquor with an ABV exceeding 0.5% at the time of sale

bank.question: What must happen to the sale of alcohol if the Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) leaves the business suddenly?
bank.explanation: Alcohol can still be sold if the DPS leaves, provided an application to vary the licence to name a new DPS is submitted immediately
options: The sale of alcohol must stop forever
The sale of alcohol can continue for up to 28 days without notification
The sale of alcohol must stop unless an application to vary the DPS is made
The store must close completely until a new DPS is appointed

bank.question: How many Designated Premises Supervisors (DPS) can be named on a single Premises Licence at any one time?
bank.explanation: A single individual can only be the DPS for one premises at a time, unless the Licensing Authority grants a specific exception (rare)

bank.question: How long is a Personal Licence currently valid for from the date it is issued?
bank.explanation: A Personal Licence is valid indefinitely unless it is surrendered, suspended, or revoked by a court or the licensing authority

bank.question: What is the minimum notice required for a 'Late' Temporary Event Notice (TEN)?
bank.explanation: A Late Temporary Event Notice must be submitted no later than 5 working days before the event, not including the notice day or the event day

bank.question: What is the legal term for an employer being held responsible for the actions of their employees?
bank.explanation: Vicarious liability means the employer can be held responsible for the unlawful actions of their employees during their work

bank.question: Who has the power to issue a summary closure order for 24 hours due to disorder on a premises?
bank.explanation: The police have the power to close a premises for up to 24 hours if there is an immediate threat to public safety due to disorder
options: A senior Police Officer (Inspector or above)

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a personal licence applicant must be, which number should the learner use?
bank.explanation: A personal licence applicant must be 18 or over.

bank.question: In APLH revision, what minimum age, in years, a person must be to give a temporary event notice, what number should be entered?
bank.explanation: A person must be at least 18 to give a temporary event notice.

bank.question: In which of the following circumstances is it legal for a 16-year-old to consume beer or cider on a licensed premises?
bank.explanation: Allowing a person under 18 to consume alcohol in a bar or pub is an offence, unless they are consuming a meal in a designated area
options: A parent or guardian is present and consents
The alcohol was purchased by an adult to be consumed with a table meal
The person is aged 16 or 17 and is drinking shandy only
The person is a staff member on their lunch break

bank.question: To which geographical area does the Licensing Act 2003 apply?
bank.explanation: The Licensing Act 2003 applies to England and Wales only; Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own distinct licensing laws
options: The United Kingdom and the Isle of Man
The United Kingdom and the Channel Islands

bank.question: The Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) must be physically present on the premises at all times when alcohol is being sold
bank.explanation: While a DPS must hold a personal licence, they do not have to be physically present at all times as long as all sales are authorised

bank.question: When applying for a new Premises Licence, which of the following must be included with the application?
bank.explanation: The Operating Schedule is a required document that outlines how the applicant intends to promote the four licensing objectives
options: A map of the local council area
A copy of the business's tax returns
A letter of recommendation from the Police

bank.question: What is the maximum number of Temporary Event Notices (TENs) a Personal Licence holder can submit in a calendar year?
bank.explanation: Personal Licence holders can submit up to 50 TENs per year, provided they do not exceed the limits for a specific premises

bank.question: What is the potential consequence for failing to pay the annual fee for a Premises Licence?
bank.explanation: A premises licence holder must pay an annual fee to the licensing authority; failure to do so results in the licence being suspended
options: A permanent ban on alcohol sales

bank.question: What notice can a Licensing Authority issue to a premises if it believes the premises are being used for the unlicensed sale of alcohol?
bank.explanation: The Licensing Authority has the power to issue a Closure Notice, typically in cases involving persistent sales to minors or serious public nuisance

bank.question: Besides the Licensing Authority, who must be notified about a Temporary Event Notice (TEN)?
bank.explanation: For a Temporary Event Notice (TEN) to be valid, the person who gave the notice must also provide a copy to the local Police and Environmental Health

bank.question: Where must a notice be displayed stating the quantities (25ml or 35ml) in which Gin, Whiskey, Vodka, and Rum are sold?
bank.explanation: Weights and measures legislation requires these spirits to be sold in 25ml or 35ml quantities, and a sign must be displayed stating which is used
options: On the front door of the premises
In a clear notice or on the drinks menu
On the back of the till receipt
Only if a customer asks to see the measurements

bank.question: Which document, submitted with a Premises Licence application, details how the applicant will promote the four licensing objectives?
bank.explanation: The Operating Schedule is a key part of the Premises Licence application that describes how the venue will be managed and how it will promote the licensing objectives

bank.question: When must a Personal Licence holder notify the court that they hold a licence if they are charged with a relevant offence?
bank.explanation: If a Personal Licence holder is convicted of a 'relevant offence', they must inform the court that they hold a licence at their first appearance
options: Only if they are given a prison sentence
When they next apply for a job

bank.question: Who is specified on the Premises Licence as being the person in charge of the day-to-day alcohol sales?
bank.explanation: The Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) must be a Personal Licence holder and is responsible for the day-to-day management of the alcohol sales

bank.question: Which of the following is NOT a licensing objective under the Licensing Act 2003?
bank.explanation: Under the Licensing Act 2003, 'smoke-free' legislation is not one of the four core licensing objectives
options: The prevention of crime and disorder

bank.question: How soon must a Personal Licence holder notify the relevant Licensing Authority if they are convicted of a relevant offence?
bank.explanation: A Personal Licence holder must notify the Licensing Authority in writing as soon as possible if they are convicted of a relevant offence
options: Only when the licence is due for renewal

bank.question: What is the minimum age for a person to be allowed on a premises used primarily for alcohol consumption without an adult?
bank.explanation: Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult in premises used primarily for the supply of alcohol, such as pubs
